newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to resurrect Wall Street tax proposals.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to resurrect Wall Street tax proposals.

text.p: President Bill Clinton is expected to resurrect a series of proposals in his upcoming budget aimed at raising revenues through closing corporate tax loopholes on Wall Street, administration officials said on Wednesday.

The proposals, which were first made last year but which were not acted on by Congress, include measures that would discourage the issuance of 100-year bonds and the use of hybrid debt/equity financing mechanisms by corporations.
"I would expect that the vast majority of the proposals will be made again," said one official, who declined to be named. "But we haven't made final decisions on everything."
One proposal that is sure to be resurrected, according to the official, is a plan to eliminate a tax avoidance mechanism called selling short against the box.
Under that mechanism, an investor arranges with a broker to sell borrowed shares of a stock he already owns, thus locking in profits but deferring taxes.

The budget, which is expected to be unveiled early next month, is also likely to propose that investors be required to use the average price of a stock bought over time in calculating their tax liability when they sell shares.
